fields.label: acoustic sounder
fields.description: A heavy transducer bolted through the hull into the ship's belly. When the gravship is landed and the sounder is powered, it can fire a sounding pulse: dust jumps from the walls, a bass note rolls through the deck plating, and for a few hours afterward the ground's reply hangs over the map as broad bands of likelihood. It never says exactly where; it says where to look. What it hears depends on the land beneath the ship.

fields.label: acoustic sounding
fields.description: Turn a landed gravship into a drum. A hull-mounted sounder drives a low pulse into the ground and listens to what comes back: water, voids, buried things, things that move. The reading is never exact, only broad bands of likelihood, and what the ground gives back depends on where you land.
